chunks: And in it that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not grant Satan authority over the believers except in the matter of the permissible (al-amr al-mubah).
So if he (Satan) comes upon them in the permissible matter, he does not exert authority over them except by His permission.
And he does not exert authority over them in the matter of what is commanded, nor in the matter of what is forbidden.
But he (Satan) calls them to good and commands them to it, and calls them to evil and commands them to it.

key_terms.الْأَمْرُ الْمَأْمُورُ بِهِ: The matter of what is commanded
key_terms.الْأَمْرُ الْمَنْهِيُّ عَنْهُ: The matter of what is forbidden

ai.seo_question: What is the extent of Satan's authority over believers according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this nuance to clarify that while Satan cannot compel believers to commit sins (obligatory acts), he still exerts influence over neutral acts (*al-amr al-mubah*) by whispering doubts or desires, thereby testing their vigilance. This distinction underscores the Shia theological view that human free will remains intact, as Satan’s role is limited to invitation and suggestion rather than coercion, a concept rooted in the verse 'He has no authority over those who believe' (13:40).
